paper.title_en: On linearly derived quantum samples for LWE
paper.abstract_en: It is known that the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem becomes easy using the Field Bernstein-Vazirani (FBV) quantum algorithm with access to quantum samples of the LWE function. We revisit a suggested route to approximate such a state: coherently superposing linear combinations of classical LWE samples and erasing the combination index register. For the full q-ary coefficient set Fmq, we show that even an ideal index-erased state does not have the required behavior: Field Bernstein-Vazirani either rejects or returns a fixed noisy translate of the secret. We then analyze more general coefficient families U ⊆ Fmq and their true-secret success probabilities. In the binary LPN case, this reveals an explicit tradeoff between sample space coverage and coefficient vector distances. Co-efficient families such as fixed-weight layers and low-weight balls yield idealized subexponential FBV repetition regimes, although these estimates exclude the cost of preparing the corresponding target states. Our analysis separates the Fourier obstruction from the state-preparation problem and provides a criterion for evaluating restricted-family constructions.
